chunks: ʿAlī narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام gave judgment regarding a man who charged at another man to kill him while the man was fleeing from him. Then another man came from the front and held him for the attacker until the man came and killed him. He ruled that the man who killed him should be killed, and he ruled concerning the other one who had restrained him for him that he should be cast into prison forever until he dies in it, because he had held him for death.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, acting as the judicial authority
key_terms.الْمَوْتِ: death, here meaning fatal consequence caused through restraint
key_terms.قَضَى: gave a judicial ruling or judgment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when one person kills and another person restrains the victim to facilitate the murder?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal judgment of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning collaborative homicide. It distinguishes between the direct killer, who is subject to execution, and the accomplice who restrained the victim, who is punished with perpetual imprisonment because he enabled the killing. The narration highlights differentiated liability in Islamic judicial rulings.
